title: The AI Moment in Drug Discovery: Daphne Koller on The Long Run - TimmermanReport.com

text:
3Nov2026

Daphne Koller is today’s guest on The Long Run.
Daphne is the founder and CEO of South San Francisco-based Insitro. It’s one of what you could call the first-generation companies that uses AI to speed up and improve drug discovery. Insitro was founded in 2018 and has secured $750 million in funding from venture capital firms and through partnerships with big drugmakers that include Bristol Myers Squibb, AstraZeneca, and Gilead Sciences.
Daphne Koller, founder and CEO, Insitro
Insitro has been collecting and curating biological data for years to get to the point where AI can be useful enough to even approach the most important hurdle in R&D – that being human clinical trials.
In this conversation, Daphne offers a reality check on what AI can and can’t do at the moment for the discovery of new medicines. She goes into specific detail about programs that her team is developing for fatty liver disease, ALS, and brown-fat driven markers with implications for cardiometabolic disease.
